clue.text: Start to be better than anyone at crossword compiling?

definitions.meaning: the beginning of something, as in 'from the very start'

definitions.text: to be better than anyone at crossword compiling?
definitions.meaning: a crossword compiler is a setter, so to outdo every other compiler is, whimsically, to beat them at setting

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their career should begin with becoming the finest crossword compiler of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented sense: 'out-' as in outrun or outdo, attached to the setter's job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a standard synonym for the beginning or commencement of an undertaking.

clue.text: Where to study time in detail

parts.note: a university, shortened to uni, is a place of study

explanation.surface: Advice on where to examine the passage of time closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In detail' looks like a phrase, but 'detail' alone is the definition, in its military sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a small group of soldiers assigned a task, which is a military squad or section.

clue.text: Wave from Victor in easy position

indicators.note: the letter for Victor is placed inside the word for an easy job

parts.note: a sinecure is a paid post requiring little work
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A gesture from someone called Victor who has landed a comfortable job.
explanation.definitionFit: The trigonometric graph of sine is the classic smooth periodic wave shape in mathematics.

clue.text: Bird, male goose, losing weight

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat

indicators.note: the word for a fool drops the letter standing for weight

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, a twit

explanation.surface: A list of birds: a male goose that has slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male goose' suggests gander, but 'goose' means a fool here, and TWIT losing W leaves TIT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small British songbird, a familiar name for the blue tit and similar species.

clue.text: Pain and deprivation for optimistic character

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
loss is deprivation of something one had

explanation.surface: Suffering and want are the lot of a cheerful fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Pangloss is the tutor in Voltaire's Candide who insists all is for the best despite every disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's tutor is the literary byword for relentless, naive cheerfulness in the face of misfortune.

clue.text: Teutons play amazingly, suppressing laugh when England generally loses?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold down, so enclose, the word for a laugh
the letters of these words are arranged in an astonishing new order

parts.note: taken as written
a hoot is a burst of laughter

explanation.surface: Germans perform brilliantly, stifling any mirth, in the familiar scenario where England go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' signals the anagram of the first two words, and 'suppressing' holds the laugh inside the result. The definition leans on England's notorious record in shoot-outs.
explanation.definitionFit: England's football team has famously been knocked out of tournaments by Germany in deciding spot-kick contests.

clue.text: Reports managed to raise tax

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
rates are a local property tax in Britain

explanation.surface: News that a government succeeded in increasing a levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns RAN into NAR. Rates were the British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or tell a story or events is to give an account of them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Organ shown by one Indian's loincloth

parts.note: a lung is an organ of the body
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A body part displayed by a man from India wearing only a loincloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cloth wrapped around the waist, worn by men in South Asia, a sarong-like garment.

clue.text: Where City workers look for sex and hire models

indicators.note: as a verb, to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped into the answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandal: bankers seeking sex and paying for models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' is London's financial district; 'models' looks like a noun but is the anagram verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial workers in London's City check a stock market index such as the FTSE to track prices.

clue.text: Picked up criminal with second name that's Brown

indicators.note: heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A criminal named Brown is arrested along with his accomplice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests arrest but means heard: SINNER, said in a non-rhotic accent, sounds like CINNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice gives its name to a warm reddish-brown colour, so the word serves as a shade of brown.

clue.text: Strip when taking off top in resort, a Gallic fashion

indicators.note: the top, so first letter, of the word resort is used

parts.note: un is French for a
a way is a manner or fashion of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone strips topless at a holiday resort in the French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' and 'taking off' suggest undressing, but they describe an airfield strip used by planes departing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft accelerates along a long paved airstrip before lifting into the air.

clue.text: Something seen in Aldi to dismay leading Tories

parts.note: to chill someone is to dismay or frighten them
the cabinet is the group of senior ministers in a Conservative government

explanation.surface: A supermarket chain deliberately unsettles senior Conservative politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain; Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarkets keep fresh and dairy goods in refrigerated display units, so one is an example of shop furniture.

clue.text: Cherry, green grass and earth? Go for another look

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red
eco means environmentally friendly, green
a grass is an informer, a rat
E is the abbreviation for earth, as in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A list of colours and textures for an interior scheme, deciding on a fresh style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To freshen up a room with new paint and furnishings is to give it a different look.

clue.text: Almost stand up or sit down on this

definitions.meaning: a horse rising onto its hind legs almost stands upright
the backside or bottom is what one sits on

explanation.surface: Indecision: half-rise or settle on one's seat instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes a horse lifting its forelegs, and the noun is a polite term for buttocks.

clue.text: Conceding close to century, fellow's out playing cricket

indicators.note: the close, so last letter, of the word century is used
the letter for fellow is put out of the cricket word

parts.note: fielding is playing cricket as the side not batting

explanation.surface: A batsman gives up near his hundred because a fielder has dismissed him.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the fielding side tries to get the batting side out.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving way or surrendering ground is a synonym of admitting defeat or allowing a point.

clue.text: Figures inspiring fighter is something to get the pulse racing

definitions.text: something to get the pulse racing

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the word for figures takes in the boxer

parts.note: digits are numerical figures
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: Numbers that motivate a boxer, and something that sets the heart thumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like motivating, but means breathing in, hence containing.
explanation.definitionFit: This foxglove-derived drug is a heart stimulant that strengthens and changes the heartbeat.

clue.text: What journalists offer is done in pen

indicators.note: the word for finished goes inside the word for an enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure, a pen
over means finished or done

explanation.surface: Reporters' work is written with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' suggests writing but is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporting on events is the news media's product, their reporting of a story.

clue.text: Giant insects besetting Henry

indicators.note: the insects surround, so enclose, the letter for Henry

parts.note: a bee is an insect
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A huge swarm of insects attacks a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: One word 'insects' supplies two different insects; 'besetting' puts the Henry letter inside the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical monster has become a general term for anything enormous, a colossus.

clue.text: Crikey! King's in anorak

parts.note: both are exclamations of surprise
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: Astonishment that a monarch is wearing a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anorak' looks like a jacket, but in British slang it is an obsessive enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an obsessive, socially awkward hobbyist matches the American term for a nerd.

clue.text: Cruel person rating one on horse, perhaps

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
horse is slang for heroin, so someone on it is a drug user

explanation.surface: A sailor who whips his horse is a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On horse' suggests riding; horse is heroin slang. A rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mistreats or harms others is a tormentor, the sense of a cruel person.

clue.text: Unable to continue racy bedroom chats

indicators.note: racy suggests lively or wild, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Steamy late-night pillow talk that leaves someone exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means 'out of the fight'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means put out of action, too badly hurt or damaged to keep fighting.

clue.text: Like some films? Loudly express despair with heads of film industry

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to sigh is to exhale in despair

indicators.note: the heads, so first letters, of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Groaning in despair alongside movie studio bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGH said out gives SCI; 'heads of' takes F and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Science-fiction is a cinema genre, so some films are described this way.

clue.text: Stay in south, returning satisfied

indicators.note: the word for satisfied comes back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: met means satisfied, as in met a demand

explanation.surface: Remaining in the south of the country, happy on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' means stop or check, not remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or check a flow, as in staunching bleeding, is to restrain or stop it.

clue.text: Daddy gets girl a fine coat

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A father buys his daughter a smart overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the thin film or sheen that forms on old bronze, wood or leather with age.

clue.text: Single to be excited about having dated

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the word for single
the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
sole means single or only

explanation.surface: A lone person is thrilled to have been on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' turns TO BE into OBTE, which 'about' wraps around SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date or outmoded is no longer in use, a synonym for old-fashioned.

clue.text: Deposit money in extremely safe organisation managing estates

indicators.note: the extremes, first and last letters, of the word safe

parts.note: a dime is a US coin
the National Trust looks after British country houses and estates

explanation.surface: Instructions to put cash into a secure property-management firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British heritage charity owning stately homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a geological or chemical deposit.

clue.text: Pick up birds outside of Exeter, heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: emus are flightless birds

indicators.note: the outside, first and last letters, of the word Exeter

explanation.surface: Collecting birds outside a city in Devon before driving west.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a city in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up again where one left off is to restart or continue something interrupted.
